Cemindia Projects Limited (previously ITD Cementation; CEMPRO / BSE 509496): Detailed analysis (Aug 2026). Trading at a modest premium to sector (P/E ~38x vs sector ~35x; market cap ~₹22,800–23,500 Cr). Strong points: record order book (~₹31,300 Cr), healthy inflows (metro, marine, tunnels, industrial, data centres, etc.), TTM EPS growth ~47%, improving project mix/margins (normalized ~10–10.5% EBITDA targeted), Adani parentage aiding opportunities/execution perception. View: Moderate further re-rating potential driven more by sustained execution/earnings growth (20–30%+ annual possible) than multiple expansion. Risks include valuation, EPC execution delays/overruns, margin normalization, and working capital. Analyst notes support strong order pipeline and growth forecasts.

Laurus Labs (#Lauruslab / #Lauruslabs)Highest multi-year conviction, frequently reiterated.  Long-standing thesis (repeated at events since Nov 2022) of market-cap growth from ~₹3,000 cr at the start of the decade toward ₹3 lakh cr. Recent posts note progress to ~₹1 lakh cr market cap by Aug 2026.  
Strong July 2026 results highlighted (“on steroids”): 62.7% gross margins, 31.8% EBITDA, 44% CDMO contribution, revenue >₹2,000 cr for the quarter, PAT ₹362 cr.  
Explicit “We are invested.” Views remained unchanged through earlier softer periods on the basis that capacities and capabilities were already built.  
Multiple high-engagement posts in July–August 2026.

2. Azad Engineering (#AzadEngineering / #AzadEngg)Very high conviction with concrete milestone updates.  July 2026: Delivery of India’s first indigenous expendable turbo-jet engine (350 kg thrust class) to DRDO (manufactured with industry partner).  
March 2026: Long-term (8-year) single-source supplier contract with Mitsubishi for complex hot-section nozzle vane segments of gas turbine engines — described as a rare achievement for an Indian precision-engineering firm and a step toward peers like Howmet.  
Emphasized unique capabilities (e.g., only Indian company among a handful globally making certain airfoil components).  
Explicit “We are invested” / “I’m invested.” High-engagement posts.

3. Axiscades (#Axiscades / #AxisCades)Repeated detailed conviction around a major business transformation.  Posts on order wins (e.g., avionics hardware for LCA Mk1A), large planned capex (Aeroland, DAC, MAC), acquisitions in aerospace/ESAI, and a bold vision in defense, aerospace, radars, missiles, UAVs, space, and electronics for global hyperscalers/consumer/telecom clients.  
Acknowledged weak recent results (deferrals, one-time charges) but framed them as temporary; compared the setup to the earlier Laurus conviction period.  
Explicit “We are invested.” Multiple substantive posts in May–June 2026.

4. Sedemac (#Sedemac)Strong deep-tech focus with multi-year preparation narrative.  Firm has studied deep tech for ~3 years and publishes related newsletters.  
Commentary on poor IPO response (undersubscribed in HNI/retail at ~₹1,350) followed by sharp post-listing gains and a global brokerage target of ₹3,700.  
Positioned as an example of sensor-less ISG technology and broader deep-tech opportunity in India.  
High-engagement posts emphasizing that understanding deep tech requires hard work but can create significant wealth.

5. Manorama Industries (#ManoramaInd)Clear long-term growth projections with personal holding disclosure.  Highlighted strong historical growth (sales CAGR ~37%, PAT CAGR ~57% over recent years; FY26 figures cited).  
Expectation of scaling to ~₹5,000 cr sales / ₹1,000 cr PAT over the next 5 years.  
Explicit “I’m invested.”

6. RNIT (micro-cap AI-related)Positive FY26 results update (revenue +60%, EBITDA +102%, PBT +127%, margin expansion to 40%).  
Explicit “I’m invested.”

Other mentions in the period include comparative notes on Aequs (valuation critique vs. Azad) and educational threads on related themes (power semiconductors/Cybertech, radar hardware, defense tech), but without the same intensity of “invested” language or repeated high-conviction framing as the above.Ranking rationale: Laurus and Azad lead due to multi-post frequency, explicit ownership statements, major operational/contract milestones, and engagement. Axiscades and Sedemac follow for transformation/deep-tech depth. Manorama and RNIT are solid but less frequently discussed in the window.

Dynamic Cables — Solid short-term setup from strong reported numbers (revenue +33% YoY, net profit +37% YoY, sharp EBITDA swing) that already drove a ~10% stock reaction in the discussion period. Smaller player with demand runway in cables/wires and relevant new products. Results-driven momentum supports near-term follow-through, though scale/liquidity may limit magnitude vs. larger names.

Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts (THELEELA) — Positive on “brilliant results,” high ADR (~Rs 20,000 corporate level), scarcity/luxury positioning, institutional backing (post-Brookfield/IPO transformation), and expansion. Hospitality recovery + premiumization supports earnings, but short-term moves may be steadier rather than explosive unless results continue surprising or expansion news accelerates.

Ramkrishna Forgings — Recovery narrative with management optimism on balance sheet improvement, sequential growth, Mexico/castings ramp, debt reduction, and longer-term targets. Post-inventory issues and tariffs, the “owning the problem” stance and improving parameters are constructive, but it remains more of a multi-quarter turnaround than pure short-term catalyst-driven name. Engagement with positive external notes supports monitoring for sequential delivery.

Shriram Pistons / SPR Auto Tech — Consistent long-term compounder narrative (noted ~80% returns over a prior year in one post), market leadership in core products, diversification (CNG, hybrids, exports, EV motors). Strong fundamentals, but discussions lean more toward sustained outperformance than fresh near-term catalysts in the latest window.

TVS Holdings — Holdco structure with large stake in TVS Motor (significant embedded value highlighted vs. market cap). Potential discount narrowing is a classic theme, but realization is often slower and more sentiment/catalyst-dependent (e.g., corporate actions) than pure operating results stories.

APSEZ / JSW Infrastructure — Structural long-term “tollbooth” thesis on India’s trade/manufacturing growth, multi-modal logistics, and capacity expansion. Strong business quality, but discussions emphasize multi-year compounding over immediate short-term catalysts. Results checks are recommended; moves more tied to broader infra/trade sentiment.
